title: String and date operators
summary: Build new text and date values inside a pipeline with $concat, $toUpper, $substrCP, $split and $dateToString.

quiz.q: What does this expression produce when `first` is 'Asha' and `last` is 'Kumar'?
quiz.explain: `$concat` joins the strings in order. The middle item is a single space.
Start at position 0 and take 3 characters: M, a, d.
`$split` returns an array of the pieces. Use `$arrayElemAt` with a position if you want just one.

quiz.q: Complete the date format so that a date prints like 2025-01-20.
quiz.explain: `%d` is the day of the month. `%Y` is the year and `%m` is the month.

exercise.task:
The `users` collection has `first`, `last`, `email` and `joined` (a date).

Write an aggregation with a single `$project` stage that outputs these fields only (no `_id`):

- `fullName`: first name, a space, then last name
- `lastNameUpper`: the last name in capitals
- `initial`: the first letter of the first name
- `domain`: the part of the email after the `@`
- `joinedOn`: the joined date as text like `2024-03-15`
hints: Everything goes inside one `{ $project: { _id: 0, ... } }`. Each new field is an expression such as `{ $concat: [...] }`.
For `domain`, split the email on `'@'` and take the element at position 1 with `$arrayElemAt`. For `initial`, use `$substrCP` with start 0 and length 1.
